description: SSOT for ALL tools (built-in + codeprovider-mcp). Entries are maintained HERE; contract fields (input/output/error/idempotency) are merged from contracts/tool-contracts.yaml by tools/harness-registry/apply-contracts.py. This file is NOT generated from contracts/tool-registry.yaml -- that file is a partial, older subset (20 of these tools).

Read.input_contract: { file_path: string(absolute), offset?: int, limit?: int, pages?: string }

Grep.input_contract: { pattern: string(regex), path?: string, glob?: string, type?: string, output_mode?: content|files_with_matches|count, -i?: bool, -n?: bool, -o?: bool, -A?: int, -B?: int, -C?: int, context?: int, multiline?: bool, head_limit?: int, offset?: int }
Grep.output_contract: { matches: string[] } | { files: string[] } | { counts: map<string,int> }

WebSearch.input_contract: { query: string, allowed_domains?: string[], blocked_domains?: string[] }

Write.idempotency_note: Same path + same content is a true no-op; same path + different content is a DIFFERENT operation and must not dedupe.

Edit.input_contract: { file_path: string(absolute), old_string: string, new_string: string, replace_all?: bool }
Edit.idempotency_note: Not replayable by design: after a successful edit old_string no longer matches, so a repeat fails loudly rather than double-applying.

Bash.input_contract: { command: string, timeout?: int(ms, max 600000), run_in_background?: bool, dangerouslyDisableSandbox?: bool, description?: string }
Bash.output_contract: { stdout: string, stderr: string, exit_code: int }
Bash.idempotency_note: A shell command's safety on replay is unknowable from its text; the key detects the repeat and hands the decision to a human.
Bash.contract_note: `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` was missing from the first version. It is the only input on this tool that changes what the call is ALLOWED to touch — omitting it from the contract hides the one field a reviewer would look for.

PowerShell.input_contract: { command: string, timeout?: int(ms, max 600000), run_in_background?: bool, dangerouslyDisableSandbox?: bool, description?: string }
PowerShell.output_contract: { stdout: string, stderr: string, exit_code: int }

Agent.input_contract: { description: string, prompt: string, subagent_type?: string, model?: sonnet|opus|haiku|fable, isolation?: worktree|remote, run_in_background?: bool }
Agent.idempotency_note: An agent run is non-deterministic; the key catches an accidental duplicate dispatch, not an equivalent result.
Agent.contract_note: `model` is an ENUM, not a free string — writing it as `string` threw away the one place this registry could have expressed the C4 model ladder as a machine-checkable constraint.

Workflow.input_contract: { script?: string, scriptPath?: string, name?: string, args?: any, resumeFromRunId?: string }
Workflow.output_contract: { runId: string, result: any, transcriptDir: string }

harness-switch-account.description: Switch active-account pointer for per-machine H6 attribution (local file write, no network)
harness-switch-account.idempotency_note: Switching to the account already active is a genuine no-op.

codeprovider-mcp.apply_patch.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, patch: string(unified diff with ---/+++/@@), strip?: int=1 }
codeprovider-mcp.apply_patch.output_contract: { applied: bool, files_changed: string[], dry_run_output: string }
codeprovider-mcp.apply_patch.idempotency_note: Dry-runs first, so a re-apply fails on context mismatch instead of double-applying. The key exists to prevent the pointless retry, not to protect the file.

codeprovider-mcp.edit_file.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, path: string, ... } (unverified)
codeprovider-mcp.edit_file.contract_note: NOT exposed by the live MCP server — the registry lists it but no schema is available, so this contract is from the registry description only. Verify or remove the entry. NO idempotency_key_pattern on purpose: a key over field names nobody has verified exist cannot be computed, and counting it toward the H2-3 threshold would inflate a criterion with a guess. Same reason `deploy:{target}:{version}` in tool-registry.yaml was useless.

codeprovider-mcp.write_file.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, path: string(relative), content: string(max 1MB) }

codeprovider-mcp.read_file.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, path: string(relative to app workDir) }

codeprovider-mcp.search_code.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, pattern: string(POSIX ERE), file_glob?: string, case_sensitive?: bool, max_results?: int=50 }

codeprovider-mcp.run_command.input_contract: { server_id: string, command: string(allow-listed binaries), confirm?: bool, timeout_sec?: int=120 }
codeprovider-mcp.run_command.output_contract: { stdout: string, stderr: string, exit_code: int }

codeprovider-mcp.exec_in_container.input_contract: { server_id: string, container: string, command: string, workdir?: string, timeout_sec?: int=60 }
codeprovider-mcp.exec_in_container.output_contract: { stdout: string, stderr: string, exit_code: int }

codeprovider-mcp.test_run.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, runner?: auto|npm|pnpm|composer|pytest|artisan, filter?: string, timeout_sec?: int=600 }
codeprovider-mcp.test_run.output_contract: { runner: string, exit_code: int, duration_sec: number, tail: string }
codeprovider-mcp.test_run.idempotency_note: Re-running tests is safe; the key exists so the pack does not re-run a 10-minute suite on an unchanged tree.

codeprovider-mcp.lint_run.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, mode?: check|fix (default check), runner?: auto|eslint|prettier|ruff|shellcheck|php-syntax, paths?: string='.', timeout_sec?: int=120 }
codeprovider-mcp.lint_run.output_contract: { runner: string, issues: int, exit_code: int, output: string }
codeprovider-mcp.lint_run.idempotency_note: mode=fix WRITES to the tree; mode=check does not. The mode is in the key because they are different operations.

codeprovider-mcp.quick_fix.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, file_path: string(relative), old_string: string(must match EXACTLY once), new_string: string, commit_msg: string, deploy?: bool=true }
codeprovider-mcp.quick_fix.output_contract: { committed: bool, pushed: bool, deployed: bool, commit_sha?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.quick_fix.idempotency_note: deploy defaults to TRUE, so a duplicate call is a duplicate DEPLOY. This is the highest-value key in the file.

codeprovider-mcp.deploy.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, skip_build?: bool }
codeprovider-mcp.deploy.output_contract: { pulled: string(commit), built: bool, restarted: bool, health: pass|fail }
codeprovider-mcp.deploy.idempotency_note: Deliberately NOT including a commit: the tool takes none, it pulls whatever is at HEAD. So two identical calls can deploy different code — the key identifies an accidental repeat, it does not promise the same result.

codeprovider-mcp.deploy_safe.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, agent_id?: string='deploy_safe', run_tests?: bool, ready_pattern?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.deploy_safe.output_contract: { lock_acquired: bool, images_snapshotted: bool, tests?: pass|fail, health_checks: 3, rolled_back: bool }
codeprovider-mcp.deploy_safe.idempotency_note: Takes an app lock itself, so a concurrent duplicate is refused by the lock rather than by this key.

codeprovider-mcp.rollback_deploy.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, confirm?: bool — OPTIONAL in the schema, enforced at runtime: the call fails without it }
codeprovider-mcp.rollback_deploy.idempotency_note: NOT a no-op on repeat: each call reverts the NEW most-recent commit, so calling twice reverts the revert. The key is what stops that.

codeprovider-mcp.git_branch.input_contract: { action: list|current|create|switch|delete|sync (required), server_id: string, app_id: string, name?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.git_branch.output_contract: { branches?: string[], current?: string, created?: bool, switched?: bool, deleted?: bool }
codeprovider-mcp.git_branch.idempotency_note: list/current/sync are read-only; create/switch/delete mutate. delete is FORCE, so a repeat on a recreated branch destroys different work — hence name is in the key.

codeprovider-mcp.git_commit.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, message: string, files?: string[]=['.'] }
codeprovider-mcp.git_commit.idempotency_note: This tool commits AND pushes. A repeat with the same message on a changed tree creates a second commit — not a no-op.

codeprovider-mcp.git_diff.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, file?: string, staged?: bool }

codeprovider-mcp.git_log.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, count?: int=10 }

codeprovider-mcp.git_status.output_contract: { branch: string, changed: string[], untracked: string[] }

codeprovider-mcp.git_push.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, branch?: string } (unverified)
codeprovider-mcp.git_push.contract_note: NOT exposed by the live MCP server — git_commit already pushes. The registry entry may be legacy; verify or remove it. NO idempotency_key_pattern on purpose, same reason as edit_file: an unverified key counted toward H2-3 inflates the criterion it is supposed to measure.

codeprovider-mcp.mysql_query.input_contract: { server_id: string, query: string, confirm_write?: bool, app_id?: string(credentials from .env), database?: string, host?: string, port?: number, user?: string, password?: string, format?: table|tsv|vertical, row_limit?: int=100 }
codeprovider-mcp.mysql_query.output_contract: { rows: any[], row_count: int, format: string }
codeprovider-mcp.mysql_query.idempotency_note: SELECT is safe to repeat; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE is not. The tool separates them with confirm_write, and this key catches the repeated write.
codeprovider-mcp.mysql_query.contract_note: `confirm_write` was missing from the first version of this contract even though the error_contract and idempotency_note below both name it. It is the flag that gates INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP — leaving the one destructive gate out of the input description is the worst single omission this file could have.

codeprovider-mcp.db_snapshot.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, description?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.db_snapshot.idempotency_note: Repeating is harmless but wastes disk; snapshots are timestamped so a repeat does not overwrite.

codeprovider-mcp.backup_create.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, target?: volume|db|dir (default volume), dir_path?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.backup_create.idempotency_note: Keeps only the 7 most recent — so repeated calls silently ROTATE OUT older backups. A duplicate is not free.

codeprovider-mcp.backup_restore.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, backup_file: string(abs path or name in /opt/_backups/), confirm?: bool — OPTIONAL in the schema, enforced at runtime: the call fails without it }
codeprovider-mcp.backup_restore.error_contract: confirm_not_set | backup_not_found | restore_failed(app data may be partial)
codeprovider-mcp.backup_restore.idempotency_note: OVERWRITES current app data. Restoring the same file twice is closer to a no-op than most, but a repeat after new writes destroys them again — hence the key.

codeprovider-mcp.http_fetch.input_contract: { url: string, method?: GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD (default GET), headers?: map<string,string>, body?: string, timeout_sec?: int=30, max_response_bytes?: int=500000 }
codeprovider-mcp.http_fetch.output_contract: { status: int, headers: map, body: string|object(json auto-parsed) }
codeprovider-mcp.http_fetch.idempotency_note: GET/HEAD are safe to repeat; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE are not, and the method is in the key for exactly that reason.

codeprovider-mcp.container_stats.output_contract: { containers: [{ name, cpu_pct, mem, net_io, block_io }] }

codeprovider-mcp.task_create.input_contract: { server_id: string, command: string, label?: string='background-task' }
codeprovider-mcp.task_create.idempotency_note: A duplicate call starts a SECOND background process; nothing downstream notices two builds racing.

codeprovider-mcp.task_get.output_contract: { state: running|done, exit_code?: int, elapsed_sec: number, buffered_output_bytes: int }

codeprovider-mcp.task_list.output_contract: { tasks: [{ task_id, label, state, elapsed_sec }] } — running plus finished within the last hour

codeprovider-mcp.task_kill.idempotency_note: Killing an already-dead task is a genuine no-op.

codeprovider-mcp.worktree_create.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, agent_id: string, branch?: string(defaults to source HEAD) }
codeprovider-mcp.worktree_create.idempotency_note: The path is derived from app+agent, so a repeat targets the same directory — the key matches that reality.

codeprovider-mcp.worktree_remove.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, agent_id: string }
codeprovider-mcp.worktree_remove.idempotency_note: FORCE-cleans if dirty, so a repeat after new work in a recreated worktree destroys it. Not as harmless as it looks.

codeprovider-mcp.note_post.input_contract: { tag: string(free-form, e.g. app_id or topic), body: string, agent_id?: string }

codeprovider-mcp.note_consume.idempotency_note: Consuming an already-consumed note is a no-op; notes are deleted after 24h.

codeprovider-mcp.note_list.input_contract: { tag?: string, include_consumed?: bool, limit?: int=50 }
codeprovider-mcp.note_list.output_contract: { notes: [{ id, tag, body, agent_id, consumed }] } — newest first

codeprovider-mcp.kv_set.input_contract: { key: string, value: string, ttl_sec?: number }

codeprovider-mcp.app_lock.input_contract: { app_id: string, agent_id: string, label?: string, ttl_sec?: int=600 }
codeprovider-mcp.app_lock.idempotency_note: Must NOT be deduped across agents — the whole point is that a second agent gets refused. Keyed by agent so one agent re-asking is the only case treated as a repeat.

codeprovider-mcp.app_unlock.idempotency_note: Releasing twice is a genuine no-op.

codeprovider-mcp.webhook_trigger.input_contract: { server_id: string, app_id: string, action?: test|test-and-deploy (default test), branch?: string='master', commit_sha?: string, author?: string }

codeprovider-mcp.cron_manage.input_contract: { action: list|add|remove (required), server_id: string, key?: string(## MCP:<key> marker), schedule?: string(cron expr), command?: string, description?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.cron_manage.output_contract: { entries?: [{ key, schedule, command }], added?: bool, removed?: bool }
codeprovider-mcp.cron_manage.idempotency_note: Keyed by marker, so add-with-same-key replaces rather than duplicating. Unmarked crons are never touched.

codeprovider-mcp.smoke_check.input_contract: { url: string, expect_status?: int=200, expect_text?: string, timeout_sec?: int=10, server_id?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.smoke_check.output_contract: { status: int, matched_text: bool, elapsed_ms: int }

codeprovider-mcp.log_scan.input_contract: { server_id: string, containers?: string, pattern?: string(default ERROR|FATAL|exception|panic|Segmentation|Traceback|Fatal|CRITICAL), since?: string='24h', case_sensitive?: bool }

codeprovider-mcp.disk_usage.output_contract: { filesystems: [{ mount, size, used, avail, pct }], heavy_dirs: [{ path, size }] }

codeprovider-mcp.cert_status.output_contract: { certs: [{ domain, expires_at, days_left }], certbot_timer: string, warnings: string[] }

codeprovider-mcp.nginx_vhost.input_contract: { action: list|get|set (required), server_id: string, domain?: string, content?: string }
codeprovider-mcp.nginx_vhost.output_contract: { vhosts?: string[], content?: string, tested: bool, reloaded: bool, reverted?: bool }
codeprovider-mcp.nginx_vhost.idempotency_note: Guards itself: backup → write → nginx -t → auto-revert on failure. Same content twice is a real no-op.
